title: Impact of Peer Ability on Academic Performance

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy

**Method: Instrumental Variables (IV / 2SLS)**

The research question asks about the causal effect of peer ability on academic performance. The key challenge is that peer quality is endogenous — students may self-select into peer groups, or unobserved factors (motivation, socioeconomic background) may simultaneously affect both peer quality and own GPA.

**Instrument:** Roommate's ability (`z`) serves as an instrument for peer quality (`x`). The identification strategy relies on **random roommate assignment**, which is common in college housing systems.

**Key assumptions:**
1. **Relevance:** Assigned roommate ability (`z`) is correlated with the peer quality/ability measure (`x`). This is testable via the first-stage F-statistic.
2. **Exclusion restriction:** Roommate assignment (`z`) affects the student's GPA (`y`) *only* through its effect on peer quality (`x`), not through any direct channel. This is plausible under random assignment since the roommate's ability shouldn't directly affect your GPA except through peer interactions.
3. **Independence (Exogeneity):** Random roommate assignment ensures `z` is uncorrelated with unobserved determinants of GPA.

Note: `z` is binary (0/1), suggesting it's an indicator for being assigned a high-ability roommate.

## 2. R Code

```r
# Load required packages
if (!require("AER")) install.packages("AER", repos="http://cran.r-project.org")
if (!require("lmtest")) install.packages("lmtest", repos="http://cran.r-project.org")
if (!require("sandwich")) install.packages("sandwich", repos="http://cran.r-project.org")

library(AER)
library(lmtest)
library(sandwich)

# ---- Read Data ----
df <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s81_data.csv")
cat("=== Data Summary ===\n")
str(df)
summary(df)
cat("\nNumber of observations:", nrow(df), "\n")
cat("Correlation matrix:\n")
print(round(cor(df), 3))

# ---- OLS Baseline (Naive) ----
cat("\n\n========================================\n")
cat("=== OLS: Naive Regression (y ~ x + controls) ===\n")
cat("========================================\n")
ols <- lm(y ~ x + controls, data = df)
summary(ols)

# ---- Reduced Form: Effect of instrument on outcome ----
cat("\n========================================\n")
cat("=== Reduced Form: y ~ z + controls ===\n")
cat("========================================\n")
reduced_form <- lm(y ~ z + controls, data = df)
summary(reduced_form)

# ---- First Stage: x ~ z + controls ----
cat("\n========================================\n")
cat("=== First Stage: x ~ z + controls ===\n")
cat("========================================\n")
first_stage <- lm(x ~ z + controls, data = df)
summary(first_stage)

# First-stage F-statistic on excluded instrument
fs_fstat <- summary(first_stage)$fstatistic
cat("\nFirst-stage F-statistic:", fs_fstat[1], "\n")
# Manual Wald test on z in first stage
fs_coef <- coeftest(first_stage, vcov = vcovHC(first_stage, type = "HC1"))
cat("\nFirst-stage (robust SE):\n")
print(fs_coef)

# Check instrument relevance
f_test_z <- waldtest(first_stage, . ~ . - z)
cat("\nWald test for instrument relevance:\n")
print(f_test_z)

# ---- 2SLS / IV Estimation ----
cat("\n========================================\n")
cat("=== IV/2SLS: y ~ x + controls | z + controls ===\n")
cat("========================================\n")
iv_model <- ivreg(y ~ x + controls | z + controls, data = df)
summary(iv_model, diagnostics = TRUE)

# Robust standard errors for IV
cat("\n=== IV with Robust Standard Errors (HC1) ===\n")
iv_robust <- coeftest(iv_model, vcov = vcovHC(iv_model, type = "HC1"))
print(iv_robust)

# ---- Wald (ratio) estimator as a check ----
cat("\n========================================\n")
cat("=== Wald Estimator (manual check) ===\n")
rf_coef_z <- coef(reduced_form)["z"]
fs_coef_z <- coef(first_stage)["z"]
wald_estimate <- rf_coef_z / fs_coef_z
cat("Reduced form coefficient on z:", rf_coef_z, "\n")
cat("First stage coefficient on z:", fs_coef_z, "\n")
cat("Wald (IV) estimate:", wald_estimate, "\n")

# ---- Robustness Check 1: IV without controls ----
cat("\n========================================\n")
cat("=== Robustness: IV without controls ===\n")
cat("========================================\n")
iv_nocontrols <- ivreg(y ~ x | z, data = df)
summary(iv_nocontrols, diagnostics = TRUE)

# ---- Robustness Check 2: Compare OLS vs IV ----
cat("\n========================================\n")
cat("=== Hausman Test: OLS vs IV ===\n")
cat("========================================\n")
# Manual Hausman-type check using control function approach
df$first_stage_resid <- residuals(first_stage)
hausman_test <- lm(y ~ x + controls + first_stage_resid, data = df)
cat("Control function approach (test endogeneity of x):\n")
summary(hausman_test)
cat("\nCoefficient on first-stage residual (p-value tests endogeneity):\n")
coeftest(hausman_test, vcov = vcovHC(hausman_test, type = "HC1"))

# ---- Robustness Check 3: Subsample analysis ----
cat("\n========================================\n")
cat("=== Robustness: Subsample by controls (above/below median) ===\n")
cat("========================================\n")
med_ctrl <- median(df$controls)
df_low <- df[df$controls <= med_ctrl, ]
df_high <- df[df$controls > med_ctrl, ]

iv_low <- ivreg(y ~ x + controls | z + controls, data = df_low)
iv_high <- ivreg(y ~ x + controls | z + controls, data = df_high)

cat("Low controls subsample (n =", nrow(df_low), "):\n")
print(coeftest(iv_low, vcov = vcovHC(iv_low, type = "HC1")))

cat("\nHigh controls subsample (n =", nrow(df_high), "):\n")
print(coeftest(iv_high, vcov = vcovHC(iv_high, type = "HC1")))

# ---- Summary Table ----
cat("\n========================================\n")
cat("=== SUMMARY OF KEY RESULTS ===\n")
cat("========================================\n")
cat(sprintf("OLS coefficient on x:        %.4f (SE: %.4f)\n", 
            coef(ols)["x"], sqrt(vcovHC(ols, type="HC1")["x","x"])))
cat(sprintf("IV coefficient on x:         %.4f (SE: %.4f)\n", 
            coef(iv_model)["x"], sqrt(vcovHC(iv_model, type="HC1")["x","x"])))
cat(sprintf("First-stage F-stat:          %.2f\n", fs_fstat[1]))
cat(sprintf("Wald estimate:               %.4f\n", wald_estimate))
cat(sprintf("Reduced form coef on z:      %.4f\n", rf_coef_z))
cat(sprintf("First stage coef on z:       %.4f\n", fs_coef_z))
```

## 3. Expected Findings

**Expected sign and magnitude:**

1. **First Stage:** The binary instrument `z` (high-ability roommate assignment) should have a **positive and significant** effect on peer quality `x`. Given that `z` is binary and `x` has a standard deviation around 0.7-1.0, I expect a first-stage coefficient of roughly 0.5–1.0, with a first-stage F-statistic well above 10 (strong instrument).

2. **IV Estimate:** The causal effect of peer ability on GPA is expected to be **positive** — being exposed to higher-ability peers should improve academic performance through study habits, knowledge spillovers, and academic norms. I expect the IV coefficient on `x` to be in the range of **0.3–0.7** (a one-unit increase in peer ability raises GPA by 0.3–0.7 units).

3. **OLS vs IV comparison:** OLS may be **biased** (likely upward if high-ability students self-select into environments with high-ability peers, or downward if there's mean reversion in peer assignment). The Hausman test will reveal whether endogeneity is a meaningful concern.

4. **Reduced form:** The direct effect of `z` on `y` should be positive and significant, confirming that the instrument moves the outcome in the expected direction.

5. **Robustness:** Results should be qualitatively stable across subsamples and with/without controls, given random assignment of the instrument.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Use assigned roommate ability as an instrument for peer quality.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: A positive causal relationship between peer ability and student GPA is identified.
